## Context / Problem

The project routing overlay (`.rebar/criteria_routing.json`, `code_review` section) can today only define standalone `project.*` criteria; it cannot extend a BUILT-IN overlay's triggers. `registry.glob_triggered_overlays` (src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:256) reads only the committed routing via `applies_to_globs` (registry.py:236), and `registry.content_triggered_overlays` (registry.py:321) is hardcoded to the deletion-impact removed-declaration regex. The parent epic's two-layer trigger design (committed high-precision tier / project noisy tier) requires a project to be able to add trigger vocabulary to a built-in overlay — starting with `concurrency`, but the mechanism is overlay-id-agnostic (a project could equally add tokens to `performance`).

## Approach

Extend the `code_review` side of the project overlay so an entry keyed by a BUILT-IN overlay id (a member of `OVERLAY_IDS`, registry.py:38) may carry two additive keys: `trigger_tokens` — a list of literal substrings matched case-sensitively against the added and removed lines of the unified diff (file headers `+++`/`---` excluded) — and `applies_to` globs, unioned with the committed globs. Consumption path (decided): these additive keys are deliberately NOT read through `effective_routing` — its built-in merge is per-key overlay-wins (`{**merged[cid], **entry}`, src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py:362), so a project `applies_to` read from the merged view would REPLACE the committed globs, the opposite of the additive semantics this mechanism needs. Instead, add a small helper in registry.py (e.g. `project_trigger_extensions(repo_root) -> dict[str, dict]`) that reads the project overlay's raw `code_review` entries directly (via the existing loader in `rebar.llm.criteria.overlay`; `_validate_routing_entry` already tolerates unknown keys, so no loader change) and returns, per built-in overlay id, the `trigger_tokens` and `applies_to` lists. `glob_triggered_overlays` and `content_triggered_overlays` union the helper's values with the committed ones, threading `repo_root` from the single call site `workflow_ops.overlay_union` (src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:98-99). `effective_routing` and its replace semantics stay untouched — it continues to govern thresholds/postures only. Positive rationale: this mirrors the plan-review side's proven project trigger mechanism (`trigger.text_all` on `project.engine-layer-enforcement` in this repo's `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`), and literal substrings — not regex — keep the gate a simple filter that is cheap to author and impossible to catastrophically misparse, matching the trigger's filter-not-finder role. ADR 0074 semantics are preserved: for `project.*` ids, empty `applies_to` still means ungated (`project_criterion_applies`, registry.py:282); for built-in ids the project keys are an additive union, so with no project entry present both functions behave exactly as today (committed `applies_to` empty still means escalation-only).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` — token-matching helper; `effective_routing` consumption in both trigger functions.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` — thread `repo_root` into the trigger calls in `overlay_union`.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py` — NEW module for the code-review trigger-extension cases (the existing `tests/unit/test_criteria_overlay.py` covers only the plan_review side of the overlay loader, and `tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py` covers the committed content trigger; neither is the right home for project-extension cases, and this module will also host the sibling stories' trigger tests).

Documentation of the mechanism is delivered by the sibling dogfood story (it documents mechanism and worked example together).

## Testing

Unit tier (pure in-process functions plus a `tmp_path` repo fixture writing a project `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`; no live boundary, so one tier lower does not exist). Oracle: the returned overlay-id lists.

- Happy path: a project entry on a built-in overlay id with `trigger_tokens: ["FROBNICATE("]` causes `content_triggered_overlays` to return that id for a diff whose added line contains the token.
- Removed-line path: the same token on a removed (`-`) line also fires.
- Glob union: project `applies_to` globs on a built-in id fire `glob_triggered_overlays` for a matching changed file that the committed globs do not match.
- Negative control: with no project overlay present, both functions return their current results — anchored on the PRE-EXISTING corpus in `tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py` (which exercises `content_triggered_overlays` with no project overlay) passing unmodified, plus an explicit no-overlay case in the new module.
- Malformed input: a non-list `trigger_tokens`, a non-string token, or an entry under an unknown id is ignored without raising.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A tmp project overlay declaring `trigger_tokens` on a built-in overlay id causes `content_triggered_overlays` to return that id for a diff containing the token on an added OR removed line; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py`.
- [ ] Project `applies_to` globs on a built-in id union with the committed globs in `glob_triggered_overlays` (both the committed-glob match and the project-glob match fire); checked by the same module.
- [ ] Negative control: with no project overlay, both trigger functions produce byte-identical results to current behavior — the pre-existing tests in `tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py` pass unmodified, and the new module asserts the no-overlay case directly.
- [ ] Malformed project entries (non-list `trigger_tokens`, non-string token, unknown id) are ignored at consumption, not raised; checked by unit test.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py` all pass.
